dedupe_keys.name: canal river trust annual boaters survey

description: The Annual Boaters' Survey of the Canal & River Trust asks licensed boaters on the Trust's canals and rivers in England and Wales how well they could navigate and how they rate the network, as evidence for the Trust's maintenance and service decisions. Coverage: the 2026 survey was sent to about one third of licence holders, chosen at random, and received 2,042 responses between November 2025 and March 2026; topics include navigation, drought-related closures, dredging, vegetation, licence costs, maintenance, communication, facilities and waste services. Overall satisfaction fell to 50% from 55% in 2025, 70% of boaters could not navigate as expected, stoppages affected 58% (15% in 2025) and 20% of the network was closed at the peak of the summer 2025 drought; the page compares with the 2025 and 2024 surveys, and a separate Boater Census Survey was run in 2022. Format and access: a web executive summary with a full PDF report. Licence and cost: free to read; no licence is stated. Caveats: survey percentages only, no microdata, and satisfaction is self-reported. The shares of boaters affected by closures can calibrate user response and service loss in inland waterway resilience and climate adaptation models of drought. It relates to the CCNR inland navigation market observation and the CCNR low-water action plan in the catalogue.
